The submitted answer is "True".

The identity ∏_{n≥1} cos(x/2^n) = sin x / x, applied with x = π/k, gives π · (k sin(π/k)/π) / sin(π/k) = k whenever sin(π/k) ≠ 0. That means the expression equals k for every integer with |k| ≥ 2, and k is an integer.

The expression is undefined at k = 0 and k = ±1, because the denominator is zero or π/k does not exist. Read as strictly "every integer", the claim fails at those three values.

The question appears to ask whether the expression is an integer wherever it is defined. It equals k there, so "True" matches that intended claim. I am accepting it on that reading.
